answers.answer: Each player takes only the chosen hero’s matching components; set hero/sidekick health to their listed starting values, shuffle that hero’s 30 action cards into a separate face-down deck, and draw 5. The younger player places their hero on starting space 1, then sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone with that hero; if the hero space has multiple zones, any of them qualifies. At setup, choose Alice BIG or SMALL when placing her and show the token. The older player then places their hero on space 2 and sidekicks under the same rules. The younger player takes the first turn.
answers.evidence: Setup: “shuffles their 30 action cards into one separate face-down deck, then draws 5 cards”; younger places on 1 and sidekicks in separate spaces sharing a zone; Alice’s BIG/SMALL choice then; older on 2; younger first.

answers.answer: Take 2 actions from maneuver, scheme, or attack. You may repeat an action, including maneuver twice, but cannot skip an action. You may hold 9 during your turn; at the end of your turn discard 2 cards to your own discard pile, leaving 7, before the opponent takes their turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “take 2 actions”; “You may repeat an action ... you cannot skip an action”; “At the end of your turn, discard excess cards ... until you have 7.”

answers.answer: Maneuver draws 1 card first, mandatorily. Then each of your fighters may move, one at a time, up to that player’s move value (plus applicable bonuses); each may choose zero. Movement follows adjacent spaces along connecting lines. You may pass through friendly fighters but not opposing fighters, cannot finish on any occupied space, and must finish one fighter’s movement before starting another’s.
answers.evidence: Maneuver: “Draw 1 card first, mandatory”; each fighter moves separately up to move value, including zero; movement restriction says may pass through own fighters, not opposing fighters, cannot finish occupied; finish one fighter before another.

answers.answer: During a maneuver, discard 1 hand card and add its printed BOOST value (the small circled number, not combat value) to the movement value for that maneuver. Ignore the discarded card’s effects. Each of your fighters receives that allowance. A defeated sidekick’s card can still be discarded to BOOST even if it cannot be played.
answers.evidence: BOOST movement passage: discard 1 card; add printed BOOST; “Ignore the discarded card’s effects”; “Each of your fighters receives that allowance”; a card unusable because its fighter is defeated can still be discarded to BOOST.

answers.answer: Do not reshuffle and cannot decline a mandatory draw. With an empty deck, the two missing cards cause two separate exhaustion events; each event deals 2 damage to every one of your surviving fighters. Thus the hero takes 4 damage and the surviving sidekick takes 4 damage.
answers.evidence: Exhaustion: “Do not reshuffle”; each required unavailable draw makes each fighter take 2 damage; mandatory draw of 2 with empty deck causes two separate 2-damage events to every surviving fighter.

answers.answer: A melee fighter may attack an adjacent opponent even across a zone boundary, but cannot attack a nonadjacent target merely for sharing a zone. A ranged fighter may attack an adjacent opponent across a boundary, and may also attack any opponent sharing a zone regardless of distance or adjacency—including a disconnected part of the same colored zone.
answers.evidence: Attack declaration: any fighter may attack an adjacent opponent across zone boundaries; melee only adjacent; ranged may also attack any opponent sharing a zone regardless of distance or adjacency, including another separated part.

answers.answer: An attack action is illegal if you have no attack-capable card in hand or none of your fighters has a valid target. Declare the attacking fighter and targeted opposing fighter. The attacker plays a legal attack card that fighter may use; the defender may decline or play a legal defense card for the defending fighter. Fighter-specific cards are restricted to that fighter; ANY cards may be used by any of your fighters. Pure defense cannot attack and pure attack cannot defend. Reveal both choices simultaneously after both are made. Versatile cards may attack or defend and count as both attack and defense cards for other effects.
answers.evidence: Attack action legality, declaration, card choice, optional defense, and simultaneous reveal are stated in Attack. Card types passage says versatile cards count as both attack and defense for other effects; fighter labels restrict use; ANY permits any fighter.

answers.answer: Resolve combat in this order: (1) IMMEDIATELY card effects, (2) DURING COMBAT effects, (3) combat result and attack damage, (4) AFTER COMBAT card effects, (5) other after-combat game effects such as a hero ability, then (6) put played cards in their owners’ discard piles. When effects share a timing, the defender resolves first. Card effects are mandatory unless they explicitly say otherwise, such as “may,” and are completed in printed order.
answers.evidence: Combat timing list gives the six-step order; “Whenever effects share a timing, the defender’s effect resolves first”; card effects mandatory unless they say otherwise; finally place cards in respective discard piles.

answers.answer: The defender wins combat: the 4 attack minus 4 defense deals 0 attack damage, and the later 2 damage from an effect does not change the combat winner. With no defense card, a value-4 attack deals 4 damage.
answers.evidence: Attack damage is attack minus defense, minimum zero; no defense means attack value. Winning combat requires the attack itself to deal at least 1; damage from effects does not change the winner.

answers.answer: A sidekick at zero is defeated and its token is immediately removed. If the game has not ended, its played card’s after-combat effect still resolves. If a hero reaches zero, that hero immediately loses and the game ends; do not continue pending effects to heal the hero or finish the turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring: remove defeated sidekick token immediately; hero defeat ends game at once. Combat timing: defeated fighter’s played card still resolves after-combat effects unless game has already ended.

answers.answer: Play a scheme face up from hand, declaring an allowed active fighter; resolve its effect, then place it in your discard pile. You cannot play it if its listed fighter is defeated. Both players may inspect either face-up discard pile at any time.
answers.evidence: Scheme: play face up; declare a fighter allowed by label; cannot play if listed fighters defeated; resolve then discard. Cards/exhaustion passage says both players may inspect either discard pile at any time.

answers.answer: Alice starts at 13 health, is melee, and has move 2. Jabberwock starts at 8 health, is melee, and shares move 2. Choose Alice’s initial BIG or SMALL size when placing her. BIG adds 2 to Alice’s attack-card values; SMALL adds 1 to Alice’s defense-card values. These size bonuses belong to Alice, not Jabberwock.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Alice 13/melee/move 2 and Jabberwock 8/melee; Alice ability gives BIG +2 attack or SMALL +1 defense and states bonuses belong to Alice, not Jabberwock.

answers.answer: Arthur starts at 18 health and is melee; Merlin starts at 7 health and is ranged. Each uses move 2 during maneuver. When Arthur attacks, he may play a hand card face down alongside his attack card and add that card’s BOOST value, ignoring its effects; discard the BOOST card. If the opponent cancels the effects on Arthur’s attack card, this ability BOOST is discarded without effect.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference gives Arthur 18/melee and Merlin 7/ranged. Arthur ability: both move 2; Arthur may BOOST an attack by adding a face-down card’s BOOST; canceled attack effects invalidate the BOOST.

answers.answer: Medusa starts at 16 health, has move 3, and is ranged. She has 3 Harpies, each with 1 health and melee attack. At the start of Medusa’s turn, she may optionally deal 1 damage to one opposing fighter in Medusa’s zone; adjacency is not required.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Medusa 16/ranged/move 3 and three Harpies at 1 health/melee. Medusa special: at start of turn, may deal 1 to one opposing fighter in her zone.

answers.answer: Sinbad starts at 15 health, is melee, and has normal move 2. Porter starts at 6 health, is melee, and uses the same move value. With 3 Voyages already in the discard pile, each may move up to 2 + 3 = 5 spaces in a maneuver before any maneuver BOOST. A newly played base-2 Voyage has combat value 2 + 3 other Voyages = 5 before other modifiers; it does not count itself.
answers.evidence: Fighter reference lists Sinbad 15/melee/move 2 and Porter 6/melee. Sinbad ability gives each fighter +1 per Voyage in discard; Voyage card gets +1 per other Voyage in discard, and played cards enter discard only at end of combat.

answers.answer: Eat Me moves Alice up to 3 spaces, then changes size. Drink Me draws 2 cards, then changes size. The size change is part of each scheme’s effect and is not stated as optional, so Alice may not refuse it after taking the first benefit.
answers.evidence: Card reference: Eat Me “Move Alice up to 3 spaces, then change size”; Drink Me “Draw 2 cards, then change size.” Effects are mandatory unless they say otherwise.

answers.answer: The attack and defense values tie at 4, so the attack deals 0 damage and Arthur wins combat. Skirmish is the defender’s after-combat effect, so it resolves before Jaws That Bite and Arthur may move Jabberwock up to 2 spaces. Jaws then checks adjacency; with no adjacent fighter, it deals no damage. If only a friendly fighter were adjacent, the Jaws damage is mandatory and Alice cannot decline to deal 2 damage to that fighter.
answers.evidence: Timing example states equal 4 values produce no attack damage and Arthur wins; defender-first Skirmish may move Jabberwock before Jaws checks adjacency. Jaws deals no damage if none adjacent, otherwise damage is mandatory even if only target is friendly.

answers.answer: At 4 health, The Holy Grail sets Arthur’s health to 8. At 5 health, nothing happens. At 0, the duel already ended upon hero defeat, so the pending healing cannot resolve to undo it. Recovery cannot raise a fighter above the highest number on that fighter’s dial.
answers.evidence: The Holy Grail: at 4 or less but not defeated, set health to 8; at 5+ nothing; at 0 duel already ended. Recovery cannot exceed dial maximum; later recovery cannot undo immediate game end.

answers.answer: Winged Frenzy lets each of Medusa’s fighters move up to 3 spaces and pass through opposing fighters. Afterward, if there is a defeated Harpy, return one defeated Harpy to any unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone; it returns one, not all. It cannot end on an occupied space.
answers.evidence: Winged Frenzy: each of your fighters up to 3 spaces; they may pass through opposing fighters; then return a defeated Harpy, if any, to any unoccupied space in Medusa’s zone; return one, not all. General rules require one fighter per space.

answers.answer: The Voyage’s value is 2 + 4 other Voyages = 6. After combat, Voyage Home returns all other Voyage cards from Sinbad’s discard pile to his hand. Home itself then goes to his discard pile at the normal end of combat. With no Voyages left in his discard pile, his next unboosted maneuver allowance is 2 spaces for each fighter.
answers.evidence: Voyages gain +1 per other Voyage in discard during combat; Voyage Home takes all other Voyage cards from discard into hand, then Home goes to discard at normal end of combat. Maneuver bonus is +1 per Voyage in discard.
